title: Commercial Marketplaces: assets, listing copy & SLA checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working draft for the minimum publishable asset pack, listing copy variations, legal/technical artifacts, and SLA/operations commitments we need to ship a Redwood Inference product listing to commercial cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP).

Context / assumptions:
- Target listing: hosted Redwood API offering (hosted inference) + 3-tier pricing (Developer / Team / Enterprise).
- We want consistent messaging across clouds but will tailor imagery, short description lengths, and required asset formats per vendor.
- This is NOT the final legal contract. Legal will supply final T&Cs and any marketplace-specific contract text.

High-level checklist (MVP for publish) — required assets and approvals:
- Product title (1) 
- Short blurb (1 sentence, 75–140 chars) — marketplace short description limits vary; produce cut at 140 and 80 chars.
- Long description (1–3 paragraphs) — includes features, use cases, platform fit, security callouts.
- 4–6 feature bullets (concise)
- 1 hero image (1200x628 PNG) + alt text
- 3 supporting screenshots (1920x1080) with callouts and caption text
- Logo (transparent PNG + SVG) – min 512px.
- One-pager PDF (product overview for listing page)
- Pricing matrix CSV (internal mapping to marketplace SKUs/pricing model)","
extra_requirements:
- Support & SLA statement (named contacts, response times, escalation flow).
- Security & compliance attestations: SOC2 Type II report link (or attestation), data residency options, KMS/HSM support description.
- Contact details for sales and support (email + landing page).
- Trial/Onboarding instructions and activation steps for free credits.
- Terms and privacy snippets per cloud (legal to provide final).
- Listing category and tags (structured list to push into marketplace taxonomy).
technical_asset_notes:
AWS: follow AWS Marketplace packaging guide — AMI or SaaS listing model? (we choose SaaS). Must provide API endpoints, sandbox credentials, and usage-based metering definition.
Azure: support for Marketplace SaaS offer, requires MPN ID, publisher onboarding screens, lead flow config.
GCP: marketplace listing needs cloud billing mapping, Google Cloud Partner ID, and a GCP-compliant privacy attestation.
Universal: include OpenAPI minimal spec (public-facing portion), sample curl/snippets, telemetry events we will surface for usage tracking.

Image and content formatting rules (quick):
- Hero: PNG 1200x628, 72dpi; avoid small text inside images.
- Screenshots: PNG or JPG, 1920x1080 and 1280x720 fallback. Add captions (plain text) for each.
- Logo: SVG preferred; provide 1 color + reversed version.
- Copy tone: pragmatic, engineering-first, short imperative bullets.

Suggested listing copy variants (do not publish verbatim yet)
- Short (<=140 chars): "Redwood Inference — predictable, high-throughput LLM inference with per-route observability, reserved capacity, and private deployment options."
- Short (<=80 chars): "High-performance LLM inference: low latency, predictable cost."
- Long (marketing paragraph): "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first runtime for serving large language models with predictable latency and transparent economics. Ship features faster using our hosted API or reserve Dedicated capacity for production SLAs. Built-in observability, intelligent batching, and automatic fallbacks help teams reduce unit-costs while preserving output quality. Available via marketplace with straightforward onboarding and enterprise-grade controls for private deployments."

Feature bullets (single-line):
- Predictable per-route SLAs and reserved GPU capacity
- Streaming and function/tool-calling support for modern agents
- Built-in batching, caching, and quantization suggestions to lower unit cost
- Per-token and per-embedding usage reporting with cost breakdowns
- Private deployment options (VPC / on-prem) and KMS integration

Pricing & SKU mapping (notes):
- Developer tier: metered, pay-as-you-go (per 1k tokens); mapped to marketplace metering dimensions.
- Team tier: committed monthly credits + burst; map to subscription SKU + usage dimension.
- Enterprise tier: reserved capacity contract (monthly seat/reservation SKU) — requires manual provisioning flow.
Action: pricing CSV template attached to repo (see linked PR) for cloud billing teams to consume.

SLA & support language (draft):
- Response times: P1 (sev 1) within 1 hour, P2 within 4 hours, P3 next business day.
- Uptime target: 99.9% for Dedicated customers; hosted API best-effort with incident page and credits policy.
- Escalation: SE -> Solutions Eng -> Eng on-call chain; provide marketplace-specific contact for lead routing.
Questions for Legal/Support: Are marketplace lead times compatible with reserved onboarding flow?

Security / Compliance checklist (MVP):
- SOC2 Type II (or in-progress with expected date) — include audit letter or attestation link.
- Data at rest encryption and KMS integration docs.
- Data egress/residency options documented per region.
- Pen test summary (redacted) and vulnerability disclosure contact.
- Privacy policy link and sample DPA language for marketplace customers.

Launch operations & lead handling:
- Lead flow: map marketplace leads to SFDC/HubSpot pipeline (owner: Ava Patel).
- Onboarding: automated onboarding email + activation steps for trial credits; include sample welcome email copy.
- Metrics to monitor post-launch: listing impressions, lead conversion, trial activation, first-call time to onboard.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Marketplace metering model across clouds: do we standardize on tokens or convert to compute-minutes for metering? (ask billing infra).
- Legal: confirm whether marketplace terms allow our enterprise SLA language verbatim.
- Pricing: need break-even analysis for each tier after SaaS fees (marketplace cut) — finance to produce.
- Technical: decide whether to publish a lightweight sandbox instance for all clouds vs. a single global sandbox.

Immediate next steps (owners assigned):
- Finalize hero + screenshot set (Noah Walker) — due 2024-11-20.
- Solidify short/long copy and 2 alt headlines (Sofia Martinez + Liam Chen) — due 2024-11-18.
- Submit pricing CSV to billing infra + finance (Ava Patel) — due 2024-11-22.
- Legal review for marketplace-specific text and DPA adjustments (Grace Kim to loop in Legal) — request by 2024-11-19.

Notes for marketplace-specific adaptions (short):
- AWS: include AWS integration notes (IAM roles, marketplace SaaS connector), meter definitions, and an AMI note if we later add Dedicated Marketplace images.
- Azure: require MPN ID and publisher profile images; confirm landing page URL formatting.
- GCP: check listing image aspect limits and provide GCP billing mapping for usage-based offers.

Appendix: example short hero headline variations to test in listing A/B
- "Predictable LLM inference — fast, cheap, and reliable."
- "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and transparent unit economics."
- "High-throughput inference + production controls for engineering teams."

This draft is intentionally pragmatic — we need to get the asset pack into the repo and unblock the cloud publisher flows. Add comments inline in the Google Drive doc; tag owners for quick follow-ups.

Unresolved editorial bits: avoid using the word "serverless" in marketplace descriptions without explicit definition; some clouds will interpret it differently.

End of draft.
